cases.question: What does the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025 say about turnover limits?

claims.text: The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 defines a small business as a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business.

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 defines a small company as a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants.

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company for VAT return purposes, the value of the person's supply of a capital asset is excluded, as is a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business.

The VAT return filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business, and a small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns.
A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns.

cases.rendered:
The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 defines a small business as a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 defines a small company as a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover"]

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company for VAT return purposes, the value of the person's supply of a capital asset is excluded, as is a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The VAT return filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business, and a small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- No Act called the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025 is among the passages; the passages come from the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025.
- The passages do not say how the two turnover limits relate to each other or which one applies to a particular business.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover" (gazette pages A 504, A 505)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10) (gazette page A 277)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-references: subsection (4), sections 105 and 107 (cited) against subsection (5), sections 100 and 102 (National Assembly). (DR-198)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-reference: section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act (cited) against section 151 (National Assembly text, the same section under its numbering, DR-000). (DR-199)

A business that ceases to be a small business shall file monthly VAT returns.
Where the Service grants an extension of the period for filing VAT returns, the extension does not extend the time to pay the tax.
Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person shall render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe.

cases.rendered:
Where a company's effective tax rate in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

This rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

"Effective tax rate" means the aggregate covered tax paid by the company for the year of assessment divided by the company's profits. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

For this section, "profits" means the net profits before tax as reported in the audited financial statement less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost for the year. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

"Multinational group" means MNE group. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "multinational group"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The top-up amount needs a calculation, which is not done here. It depends on the company's profits as defined in section 57, the covered tax paid, and the 15% target rate.
- The passages do not say whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or what makes a group an MNE group.
- The passages do not give the audited net profit before tax, or the depreciation and personnel cost figures, needed to work out profits as section 57 defines them.
- Section 57 refers to "covered tax", and the passages do not define that term.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "multinational group" (gazette page A 506)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.question: Our company gave money to a church school's building fund. Can we deduct that donation, and is there a limit?

claims.text: For working out a company's profits or loss from any source chargeable with tax under Chapter Two, the amount of any donation the company makes for that period to a fund, body or institution in Nigeria to which section 164 applies shall be deducted.
Section 164 applies to donations made to religious, charitable, educational and scientific institutions established in Nigeria, as well as to public funds and statutory bodies or institutions.
A donation under section 164 may be deducted from the profits of that period even if the donation is of a revenue or capital nature.
A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide the requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority.
The total deduction allowed to a company under section 164 for any year of assessment shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year.
For a donation other than in cash, the value for section 164 is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired.
Section 164 is subject to its own provisions and applies despite anything in section 20.

gaps: The passages do not say whether a church school counts as a religious or educational institution established in Nigeria, or whether a gift to its building fund is a donation to such an institution.
The calculation of the 10% limit on the company's actual profit before tax is not done here.

cases.question: Our company supplies feed gas to a gas processing plant. Do we charge VAT on it?

claims.text: The supplies listed in section 186(1) are exempt from the VAT imposed under Chapter Six of the Act, and that list includes crude petroleum oil and feed gas for all processed gas.

cases.rendered:
VAT is paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 145]

VAT is charged on the value of all taxable supplies at the rate of 7.5%, subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 148]

The value of an imported taxable supply is the price of the taxable supply imported plus two kinds of additions. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 150]

The first addition is taxes, duties and other charges levied either outside Nigeria or by reason of importation into Nigeria, other than VAT imposed under the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 150]

The second addition is costs by way of commission, parking, transport and insurance up to the port or point of entry. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 150]

Where a taxable supply is for a money consideration, its value is the amount which, with the VAT chargeable added, equals the consideration. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 149]

Where a taxable supply is not for a money consideration, its value is its market value. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 149]

Both the charge to VAT and the rate are subject to Part IV of Chapter Eight, which deals with exemptions from VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 145; Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 148]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether machine parts, or the specific goods being imported, are a taxable supply or are exempt.
- The passages do not set out the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight, apart from the definition of machinery, so whether any exemption applies cannot be determined.
- The passages do not say how the definition of machinery relates to the goods being imported.
- Working out the actual VAT amount on the import needs a calculation that is not done here.

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s72 subsections (2) to (4): banks and government bodies demand a certificate for the three years before the current year of assessment for the listed transactions.
cases.question: Why would my bank ask for a tax clearance certificate, and how many years must it cover?

claims.text: Any commercial bank with which a person has any dealing in respect of the transactions listed in subsection (4) shall demand from that person a tax clearance certificate of three years immediately preceding the current year of assessment.

The listed transactions are: an application for a certificate of occupancy, approval of building plans, an application for award of a contract by government or its agencies, an application for a firearms licence, an application for an import and export licence, and an application for a trade licence.

A tax clearance certificate shall disclose, for the last three years of assessment, total profits or chargeable income, tax payable, tax paid, and tax outstanding or alternatively a statement that no tax is due.

gaps: The passages do not say whether a bank asks for a tax clearance certificate for other dealings, such as opening an ordinary account, or for a particular transaction of the asker.
Whether the asker's dealing with the bank is one of the listed transactions is not stated in the passages.

A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000.

A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government.
A person engaged in banking, insurance, stock-broking or other financial services in Nigeria shall ensure that every taxable person provides a Tax ID.

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company, and for a small company the rate is 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Any company other than a small company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The question text includes a passage-like statement giving a different rate. It is part of the question, not a supplied passage, so it is not relied on.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)

cases.question: We bought ₦9 million of office furniture. How much capital allowance can we claim each year?

claims.text: Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is a type of qualifying capital expenditure.
Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2 of Table I, which has a rate of 20%.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business, at the rate specified in Table I.
The allowance is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person owns the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.

The residue of a qualifying expenditure at any date is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before that date for the asset, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date.

An allowance is not made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
An allowance not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business is carried forward to a subsequent period.

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the year, and any part that cannot be fully deducted for lack of remainder is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised.

gaps: The yearly amount needs a calculation applying the rate to the cost and the residue, which is not done here.
The passages do not say whether the furniture is used wholly for the business, whether the cost is wholly qualifying expenditure, or what the basis period is for the business.
The passages do not say whether the allowance in later years is worked on the original cost or on the residue.

Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is a type of qualifying capital expenditure. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraph 1, definition of "qualifying capital expenditure", paragraph (j)]

Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2 of Table I, which has a rate of 20%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, Table I, Capital Allowance]

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business, at the rate specified in Table I. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

The allowance is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person owns the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

The residue of a qualifying expenditure at any date is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before that date for the asset, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

An allowance is not made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

An allowance not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business is carried forward to a subsequent period. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the year, and any part that cannot be fully deducted for lack of remainder is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, and subject to section 67, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of the tax payable is added to it. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

For naira remittances, the unpaid tax carries interest at the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread to be determined by the Minister, from the date the tax becomes payable until it is paid. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

For foreign currency remittances, the unpaid tax incurs interest at the prevailing Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") or any successor rate, plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines, from the date the tax becomes payable until it is paid. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The interest under section 65(1)(b) and (c) is compound interest. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The penalty and interest under section 65 are not deemed part of the tax paid for the purpose of claiming relief under the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The relevant tax authority may, for any good cause shown, remit the whole or any part of penalty or interest due under the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 66]

- The calculation of the 10% sum and of the interest on the tax amount over the period of lateness is not done here.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person that fails to process a taxable supply through the fiscalisation system is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦200,000 plus 100% of the tax due and an interest at the prevailing Central Bank of Nigeria Monetary Policy rate per annum. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 104]

The Act says "tax" includes any duty, levy or other revenue accruable to the Government in full or in part under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025, or any other law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "tax"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not define "taxable person", "taxable supply" or "fiscalisation system".
- The passages do not say who assesses or collects the penalty, or how it is imposed.
- Working out the total amount payable in a particular case needs a calculation, which is not done here.
- The passages do not say how the interest rate is fixed or which Central Bank of Nigeria rate applies at a given time.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 104 (gazette page A 312)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "tax" (gazette page A 331)

cases.rationale: nta2025:s202:def:small-company (turnover ₦50,000,000 or less, fixed assets not above ₦250,000,000, professional services excluded) and nta2025:s56 (0% small company, 30% others).
cases.question: My company sells furniture, has turnover of about ₦30 million a year and fixed assets worth ₦40 million. What company income tax rate applies to it?

claims.text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%.
Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of this Act.
A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

A separate effective tax rate rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. Where such a company's effective tax rate is less than 15%, it shall recompute and pay additional tax that makes the rate equal to 15%.

The passages do not say whether the turnover and fixed asset figures in the question are the gross turnover per annum and total fixed assets the definition uses.

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of this Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A separate effective tax rate rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. Where such a company's effective tax rate is less than 15%, it shall recompute and pay additional tax that makes the rate equal to 15%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether selling furniture is a business providing professional services.
- The passages do not say whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group.
- The passages do not say whether the turnover and fixed asset figures in the question are the gross turnover per annum and total fixed assets the definition uses.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s73(1)-(4): advance rulings on application by a taxable person, issued within 21 days or with written reasons.
cases.question: Can my company ask the tax service for a written ruling on how a law applies before we go ahead with a deal?

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, where the ruling does not amend or replace the law.
The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling on application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give written reasons for being unable to issue the ruling.
An application is made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to a tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more such parties.

The definition of advance ruling includes a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction or proposed transaction, with a view to giving direction or clarification.

The application must contain listed details, including the taxpayer's name, Tax ID, postal address, email address and telephone number, a complete description of the issue or transaction and its financial implications, if any, and the impact on tax liability.

The application must also contain details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions on the issue, the legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.
The tax authority may ask the applicant for more information and, where necessary, shall give a reasonable opportunity to make representations or clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on foreign law, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or connected persons.
A ruling is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, and is rendered on a set of facts before the tax authority and cannot be of general application.

An advance ruling is void where the transaction actually carried out is materially different from the one described, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption or condition set by the tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerns is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation it is based on.

gaps: The passages do not say that a company is a taxable person or a party who may apply for a ruling, so that link is not stated.
The passages do not say which body is the relevant tax authority for a given tax.
The prescribed form and manner of applying are not among the passages.
